prior_importants.description: A branch that only deletes a real binary of a format outside BINARY_FORMATS (a .pdf, .gif, .woff2, .webp, .zip), or a PNG/JPEG over 1 MiB, now recounts its newline bytes as deleted source lines and names the file in `forged`. Before this PR it answered null. Nothing reaches the tree, so this is a false forged flag, and the bogus count can also trip the oversize flag.

findings.description: A `.gitattributes` `working-tree-encoding` attribute rewrites a known-binary blob on checkout, so a blob that passes the ICO/TIFF/MKV/TTF magic and zip/phar/tar refusals is checked out as a real zip or phar, carrying uncounted compressed source past the diff-size gate.

A gitlink (160000) side is read as a blob. If a branch swaps a binary file for a submodule at the same path, or a submodule for a binary file, `cat-file -s` or `git diff <blob> <commit>` throws, and the merge gate errors on every re-gate. Before this change the old code skipped that entry.
findings.body:
**Concern.** A binary file and a submodule can trade places at the same path, for example a committed prebuilt `vendor/libfoo` replaced by a submodule, or the reverse. Tree-diff then reports one typechange pair (`T`). Only a file against a directory is split into a delete and an add, and a gitlink is not a directory. Numstat prints `-\t-` for the pair because its blob side is binary. The `--raw` sides become `{mode: '160000', oid: <submodule commit>}` and `{mode: '100644', oid: <blob>}`. Nothing filters gitlinks before the recount (`rawSide` drops only the all-zero mode, and `countChangedLines` filters only lockfiles). `gitDiffBinaryRecount` then treats both sides as blobs:

```ts
const size = blobSize(repoPath, side.oid);          // cat-file -s <commit oid>
if (!mayBeKnownBinary(side.mode, size)) return false; // mode checked only after the read
```

```ts
for (const hunk of diffHunks(repoPath, [baseBlob.oid, branchBlob.oid])) {
```

**Trigger.**
- If the path names a format (e.g. `x.png`), `blobIsKnownBinary` runs `cat-file -s` on the submodule commit before the mode check. That commit lives in the submodule's own object store, so the read fails.
- Otherwise `sideOf` returns `false` and the recount runs `git diff <commit> <blob>`. That fails with a bad object, or is refused because it mixes a commit with a blob.

**Consequence.** The error propagates out of `countChangedLines` and `measureBranch`. The gate errors on every re-gate of that branch, and there is no forged flag the operator can accept. Before this PR, `blobIsBinary` returned true for the binary side and the entry was skipped. No test pairs a gitlink with a `-\t-` entry. The only gitlink assertion is `mayBeKnownBinary('160000', 10)`.

**Fix direction.** Treat a 160000 side as having no blob before reading anything. Either count only the blob side's lines with `blobLines`, as an add or a delete is counted, or skip that side. In `blobIsKnownBinary`, check the mode before calling `blobSize`.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/11dc7be7928b66ed3b594c80363d5d3e7d6d9c3e/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L1184-L1200

process_issues.description: Round 5 importants-only budget: conventions, docs, context, simplicity and maintainability were skipped. Spec was skipped because no closing issue or --spec source exists, and workflow-safety because no .github/workflows file changed. Correctness and security each ran two instances because the diff is about 1,800 added lines. Under the round-5 budget, reviewers' minors were not recorded: a PHP old-format (257-byte checksum) tar header passing opensWithTarHeader for a `.tar.png` name, at the same impact ADR 0154 already accepts; readBlobs' exact maxBuffer also counting stderr; diffHunks passing blob oids without a trailing `--`; one 64 MiB cap shared across a filesNaming batch, a cost the ADR declares; and the filesNaming JSDoc still saying a listed path the tree does not hold 'refuses'. The guards reviewer noted that git-blobs.client.ts and git-diff.client.ts import each other; no guard checks for cycles.
